utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's for "bodies." All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance, Your Honour. Could we just erase this spot where the witness indicated that the bodies were located, and could we give the witness the possibility of marking the spot again? As just described by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Because he said they were on the asphalt surface. All right. So, usher, help him please delete that circle from where it is, so that he puts it again where he thinks it was, or it should be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you estimate how many bodies in total you saw there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the site I have marked with a spot, I saw five people being killed by this man in camouflage uniform and at the other location there was a pile of perhaps -- well, it's difficult to say whether there were 40 or 50 bodies there, but something like that. There were 40 or 50 bodies at the most, no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see in the photograph, in the central part of the photograph, there is an open area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From the road were you perhaps able to see, in that part of the complex, that there were detainees being held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see that. Either there weren't any there at the moment when I was passing by, or I didn't notice. But I really wouldn't know whether they weren't there or I simply didn't notice them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned on Friday the fact that you saw about 10 or 15 or perhaps even 20 men in camouflage uniforms. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the spot at which you saw these men in camouflage uniforms? The spot that they were roughly present at.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll mark the spot where there was this man killing these five men. There were two or three here, there were some here. That's where there was a group of soldiers, and around here the spot where this man was killing the men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to be specific. Can you put against -- or to the left of the spots where you said you saw soldiers killing the men, can you put -- write the letter S, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the other dots that you put to the left of 5K, is that also meant to indicate the presence of soldiers killing those five men or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What are those supposed to indicate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The soldiers, but they didn't participate in the killing of these five men whom I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Then can you then write to the left OT, meaning other soldiers. OS, not OT. OS, yes. Other soldiers. To the left of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In front of number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, to the left of those dots.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, correct. OS. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. I'm sorry to interrupt you like this, but I think it makes things easier to follow later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's conclude with this now. You marked the spots at which the soldiers were, and they were right -- to the right of the X, and these are the sites where people were executed but these soldiers are not soldiers who participated in the execution. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that a group of 15, 20 or 15 or 20 men were wearing various times of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could see at the time, they were all wearing green camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we agree that the distance between the road and the complex itself, I'm referring to the road that you were on at the time, could we agree that the distance between the road and the complex is at least 30 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we agree that this road is separate or separated from the warehouse itself by a path, wire fence and an -- a car park, an asphalt car park in front of the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And this photo confirms that, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will no longer need this photo. Therefore, I would kindly ask the witness to put today's date in the right lower corner. And today we are 27 March. And can he also put his initials, PW-161.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would also kindly thank the usher. Later on we will need another document, and that's when we will need her again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You stayed in front of the warehouse for just a short while, and then you continued on your way to Konjevic Polje. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you spend any time in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stayed there for a very short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the check-point of the civilian police there, as you call it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This may be an opportunity to skip a few events here, because you mentioned the civilian police when you said that you saw them in front of the buses. My question will be this: How do you know that those were civilian policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they wore blue uniforms. The classical blue uniforms usually worn by those lads from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just, if we could clarify, is he talking about the ones in front of the buses or the ones in Konjevic Polje? I don't think it's clear from the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which ones are you talking about, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I will take it step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In Konjevic Polje you saw a check-point of the civilian police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Those were policemen wearing blue, classical police uniforms from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you have also told us that you saw civilian policemen in front of the buses in Bratunac when they had arrived bringing civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the evening before that. The evening before that there were buses in front of the municipal building, there were three buses. I and Davidovic were giving people water. I can't remember whether there were one or two police officers there, there were civilian policemen wearing blue uniforms, classical uniforms. And on the following day, not only in Konjevic Polje, but also in -- near Glogova to Kravica and from Kravica to Konjevic Polje, there were three or four police check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Those were members of the police station in Bratunac, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew almost all of those lads.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not sure, but now that I've mentioned the name on page 61, line 4, maybe this should be redacted. Although it seems to me that this name has not been redacted in the past, but I'm still -- I want to be certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Unless someone disagrees, strongly disagrees with this. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On your way back from Konjevic Polje and Sandici, you saw a column of vehicles by this special police. I am quoting from transcripts on Friday, and this column was moving very fast past you so that you had to stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: A civilian policeman told you that Zvornik was about to fall, and that this special unit of the police was sent to defend Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but before that I asked the policeman who those men were and why they were in such a haste and then he said that the -- Zvornik was about to fall and the special police had been sent to defend Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that this was in the early evening hours of that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I was returning. This was at dusk.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that on that occasion you saw the uniforms on the members of the special police that were on their way to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wore camouflage uniforms. Overalls, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The uniforms of the persons whom you saw in front of the warehouse were green and not of the same colour as on the members of the special police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those uniforms were dark green, and I don't know whether the shirts were short-sleeved or whether their sleeves were rolled up. I can't tell you at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Had you previously seen patches of the special police brigade on the sleeves of those uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The men whom you saw in front of the Kravica warehouse who participated in the execution did not have any patches on his sleeves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did not even have the insignia of the army of Republika Srpska. His sleeves were either rolled up or short. I can't tell you which. In any case, the sleeves were short. And the colour of his uniform was dark green.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's try and clarify one thing for the transcript. Am I right in saying that the policemen, i.e. the special police whom you saw in uniforms on their way to Zvornik, were not dressed the same as the person whom you saw participating in the execution in front of the warehouse. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are. The uniforms were not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Bratunac, at one point that evening you met up with Ljubomir Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And in the transcript on Friday you say that he had been ordered to go to Zvornik urgently and that you established a link between that and the column of the special police that you had previously met. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have also mentioned that one of the people who were present there in your group had heard and had spoken about one of the Muslims having grabbed a rifle from a policeman and killed him by firing a burst into him and that another policeman grabbed the rifle barrel and burned his arm. That's on page 3964 of transcript on Friday. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was the case. This is what we discussed when we met up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have also told us that you don't know where this incident happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You also don't know the names of the policeman who was killed and the other one who was hurt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe this is a good moment for us to see Exhibit Number P01892, which is in e-court. I would like to call it up. This is a document which is in both English and B/C/S, and this is an excerpt from the register of patients from the Bratunac Brigade. Can we look at page 0179-3920? This is the ERN number of the page. While we are waiting for the document to be shown, let me just correct in transcript, this is an expert [as interpreted] from the register of patients of the Bratunac hospital, rather than the Bratunac Brigade, and I would like to correct that in the transcript. Thank you. Can this be blown up in B/C/S, and can we also have the English version on the screen at the same time? In English this is on page number 2. This can be found on e-court. If not, I have just been told that it is on e-court, and I will kindly ask for the English version to be put on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can find it ourselves in English. The witness doesn't need to see it in English. So let's proceed with what we have on the monitor. If everybody is in agreement, because...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let us look together. Column, or rather row 1490, which is the second from the top, it says here that on the 13th of July, 1995, at 1740 [as interpreted], a patient by the name of Rade Cuturic, father's name Milan, born on the 26th of August 1990 -- 1971 was admitted. He was a member of the special brigade of the MUP. His wounds are registered in the last column, it says here burns of inner side of the palms between the second and the fourth digit of the left hand with lacerations and the therapy is listed. Can you see all that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at row number 1491. It says that on the 13th of July, 1995, at either 1800 or 1900 hours, which is not very clear in the B/C/S version, in the English it says that it was at 1800 hours, another person was admitted. His name is Krsto Dragicevic, father's name Bogoljub. He is from Skelani, a member of the special police unit, and it is stated here that he was killed. The Latin diagnosis is in this line. Can you see this, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It is stated here that they were both wounded in Kravica. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is this: Judging by the chronology of the events and the description of wounds, could these two persons be the ones that were involved in the incident that you had heard about during your meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And finally, I would kindly ask you to look at 1489, the first line from the top. It says here that on the 13th of July, 1995, at 1730, Miroslav Stanovic was brought to the hospital. He is from Srebrenica, a member of the Red Berets. He was wounded in Kravica. And it says under the diagnosis that he was wounded in the left -- right lower arm, that he has a gun-shot wound, and that it also has some wounds on the face and that he was referred to the surgical department in Zvornik. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is this: Do you know who Miroslav Stanovic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it says Miroslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Miroslav.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know several people by the name of Stanovic, but I don't know Miroslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in 1995 the Bratunac Brigade had an intervention unit that was referred to as the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would kindly ask the usher to assist us and to put a document on the ELMO a document. Your Honours, I apologise, this document has still not been placed on e-court, but it has been submitted to our learned friends from the Prosecution. This is page 11 of the magazine called,"Policeman," published in August 1994. An article was published in that issue and the title is, "Police Officers With Office Titles."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Published in 1994, I think that may be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what it says, "Policeman" published in August 1994. If you show me the parts, I can -- yes, let's proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This was published in August 1994, we can see it in the right bottom corner. This the only thing that we were able to locate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I will kindly ask the witness to look at this article. The last person on the right-hand side, and the caption is, "Rado Cuteric." That is the name that we have just seen in the records of the hospital. My question is this: Can you remember whether this person, whether this man came with his hands wrapped up? Did he join you when you were sitting down with that group of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recognise him in the photo, but a lad wearing a black T-shirt, a handsome lad of medium build and height, with his hands wrapped up was sitting with us and we had been waiting for him. It says here that he was admitted at 1740 hours, and he joined us at the Jasen restaurant an hour or so later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This would be all regarding this photo. And now I would like to ask you this: We had an occasion to hear several witnesses, Bosniaks, in this courtroom, who were in the meadow in Sandici and Lolici on the 13th and the 14th of July, 1995. They have told us that in the course of the day, a cistern came, bringing them water and splashing them with water to refresh them. To my colleague's question, you confirmed earlier today that the cistern belonging to your company did go to that road on those days and took water to the prisoners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't believe there is any evidence in the record that there were any live Muslims on that meadow on the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What do you have to state about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can provide a reference for the witness who spoke -- to be told about the 13th and since he was a protected witness, I will focus on the 13th, if I may be given that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 13th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you maintain then your objection if it's limited to the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No problem with the 13th. The 14th is...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I thought. So if you limit yourself to the 13th, Mr. Stojanovic, we can proceed. Otherwise, I think we'll need to check properly, because I think Mr. McCloskey is correct. So go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I do have a reference for the 13th, and my question for the witness is this:

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who gave you the task to send your cistern to that road, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that from the army or from the civilian authorities, if you can't remember exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't say off the top of my head, because I can't remember. There was a cistern. It went to Bratunac on a number of occasions to fill up with water and then it returned to the same location.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned your meeting with Ljubomir Borovcanin that evening. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long that meeting lasted, approximately, how many minutes, how many tens of minutes, how many hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the following day, as you testified on Friday, you spent the greater part of the day in Glogova and you monitored the work of the machines. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point in time you went to Konjevic Polje again on that day. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you be more precise and tell us what time of day it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You passed by the Kravica warehouse again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you spend any time there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any machinery in front of the warehouse on that day in the afternoon hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ULT wasn't there in Glogova anymore, perhaps it was in Kravica, but I didn't pay much attention to this. I didn't see it. But I didn't have it in Glogova, at the location in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers at that point in time in front of the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay much attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just like to put a few more questions to the witness, and then I will conclude, but could we please move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And in these graves in Glogova, all the bodies that were found in Konjevic Polje were buried there too; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Bodies found, when searching the territory and the area of Radno Buljek [phoen], Kamenica, Pobudje, these bodies were also buried there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those who were killed up there, and even the five or six bodies that I saw by the Vuk Karadzic School, the driver later informed me that there had been more of them. All of them had been taken and -- to those graves and buried in those graves in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Glogova or those graves in Glogova were places where all these bodies were buried?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is at a location on the left and the right to the road to Kravica, and what Momir said about the area in the direction of Halilovici, we weren't involved in that. I don't know who was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say Momir mentioned this, you are referring to Momir Nikolic, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think we can take the break now, five minutes ahead of schedule. Can we have more or less an estimate? I think you have already intimated that you have cut down your hour to about 40 minutes, Madam Fauveau? And the Gvero Defence team? Yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that we won't need much time for the cross-examination of this witness. We believe that we'll need less than 30 minutes, and we hope to conclude -- we hope that all the Defence teams will conclude by the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I have a problem with the microphone. We will have 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 10 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think we'll need more than 25 or 30 minutes and I believe we will be able to conclude by the end of the day. I will do my best to be as brief as possible, and to conclude today. It depends on how lengthy the answers are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's make -- do you think you will have a re-examination, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Very briefly. And I think if we could really insist that this gets done by the end of the day. The time from direct to cross in this context really is beyond the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll come back on that and I'm sure that you will think it over and do your best to finish this witness today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you all agreed to finish with this witness today? All right. Then we will not try to cut down ourselves, establish what, a time limit? Use your best judgement respecting each other. And, of course, Mr. McCloskey too. Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we first move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are already in open session. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Such a company also existed in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was therefore involved in the production and supply of water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to some information that I have, sources and pumps to supply the Srebrenica water-supply system were in Zeleni Jadar. Are you aware of the fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is the Zeleni Jadar area to the south of Srebrenica, and after the safe haven was established, was that area under the control of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During the wartime years, did you hear anything about Serbian forces, soldiers or police forces or any other forces, did you hear anything about them committing sabotage on that water-supply system, and as a result they threatened to cut off the water-supply to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Potocari, which is a village in the vicinity of Srebrenica, it's several kilometres from Srebrenica in the direction of Bratunac, was not linked to the urban water-supply system, to the town water-supply system?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Potocari was linked to the Srebrenica water-supply system.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As for the villages in the enclave, I don't want to enumerate them now, but they include Suceska, Bojna, Vutuzarevo, and other villages, did these villages have their own independent water-supply systems in the area, in their respective areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Srebrenica, as in all other municipalities, in addition to the town water board, there were village water boards, village water-supply systems. Each and every hamlet, each and every village had their own source. There were even houses that had their own sources of water, they had their own springing and they used them so to supply themselves with water.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So the army of Republika Srpska could in no way pose a threat to the supply of water to Srebrenica or the entire enclave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, naturally it couldn't because it was all under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very briefly now, Bratunac, tell me, how did Bratunac obtain water in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 Bratunac used the main town water board from Bjelovac for its needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that water-supply system blown up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on three occasions, and the reservoir on one occasion. So that's a total of four occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the ABiH did this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, there's another subject I would now like to move on to. You have already spoken about it at length, but I'm interested in the time when you returned on the 13th, the 13th of July. We are certain about that now. You returned in the evening hours from Kraljica [as interpreted] to Bratunac, you returned to Bratunac, you passed through the town and you went to the Javere [phoen] restaurant in the evening. You went there about 9.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Jasen restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It got translated as Kraljica or something like that. And I know you didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He said Kravica anyway. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When passing through the town did you notice any army members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day when what happened in Kravica happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you returned to Bratunac from Kravica, and you passed through the town. When passing through the town did you notice any members of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the army or rather the units that participated in combat operations in the vicinity of Srebrenica withdrew and they went to another location in the direction of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that a unit or rather the soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade were deployed at positions that were not in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the town only the members of the local Bratunac police remained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have spoken about the 14th of July, that in the morning you were informed about some five or six bodies, and that the driver, Cvetinovic, informed you that he had transported those bodies to Glogova?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That was in the morning hours of the 14th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After having received that information, on the 14th in the afternoon on the 15th, and later on, did you see or heard about any killings that happened at the school, in the hangar and at the Vuk Karadzic School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the year 2000 you were together with Mr. Ruez, you escorted him to certain localities that he was interested in. And those localities were all relative to your statement, given in October 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Ruez ask to enter the hangar, the Vuk Karadzic School, and the technical school when the two of you visited Bratunac and its surroundings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Petrusic, also for your cooperation. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'll have a few questions for you about something that you have already tackled in your evidence, and it concerns -- they concern your stay in Srebrenica in the town after the units of the Drina Corps had entered the core. Were you in Srebrenica a few days after that? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Srebrenica maybe 10 days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an occasion to see the town, the centre of town itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I inspected the entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an occasion to see the hospital, the post office building, the municipal building, and the Bela [phoen] base which had been the United Nations base in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see the post office, the hospital, and what other buildings did you mention?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The United Nations base in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entrance to the town?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And did you notice on these buildings any bullet or shell traces? What was the condition of these buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any shell traces, the facades were not damaged by shrapnel. There might have been some bullet holes like on all the other buildings, but they were the result of the fighting at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your view those were old bullet holes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Old damage. Did you have an occasion to see that the unit had cleaned the United Nations base? Did you have an occasion to enter the United Nations base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did enter, but the units did not. And we did not clean Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the base itself, did you see any shell holes or blood indicating that something had happened there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Mr. Krgovic. Thank you so much. Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: You had a function in the civilian protection of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the commander of the civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Maybe, yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think this needs to be redacted and we will go into private session if you're pursuing that line of questioning, Mr. Sarapa. That line of questions

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how was the civil protection of Bratunac organised and in Republika Srpska for that matter, according to what principle was it organised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how it was organised in Republika Srpska. In Bratunac the military department mobilised people, mostly men who were not able-bodied, to organise civilian protection unit. They cleaned the terrain, both in peacetime and in wartime.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Did all members of the civilian protection have their assignment in the civilian protection, a constant assignment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: You have mentioned the task of cleaning. What is that? What is this task, cleaning? In very short outlines, if you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilian protection exists in all countries and it is well-known why it exists. In wartime conditions they exist to bury the dead, the killed, the animal carcasses, and prevention of contagious diseases for the removal of various obstacles on the river-banks, on roads this is what you call sanitisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Can you make a distinction between a general sanitisation and the battle field sanitisation or clean-up of terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The clearing of the battle field or hygiene and sanitation measures of the battle field, you know what this is, the civilian protection has to remove bodies, bury them, mark the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Does this mean that civilian protection units from Bratunac were also involved in the clearing up of the battle fields?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Can you please tell us whether the civilian protection was part of the Republika Srpska army, or was it an independent organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the wartime conditions the civilian protection serves military purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific? Was the civilian protection a part of the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Who did the civilian protection receive requests from, or tasks? To be more specific, the clearing up of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: In the wartime conditions there were no requests, there were just orders which needed to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: When we are talking about this type of requests that come directly from military structures do you think that this is in keeping with the regulations, that this is by the book as it should be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: On the 22nd --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 26th, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Or rather yesterday when answering the Prosecutor's questions about the excavator, you said this on page 15, line second -- line 2, you are talking about a backhoe excavator.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we should go into private session at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Witness, are you aware of the area mentioned by Mr. Stojanovic called Ravni Buljum?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ravni Buljim. I know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that out in the woods beyond Jaglici in a rather remote area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's somewhere in the woods, and there are houses up there too. Ravni Buljim is a very wide area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: During the days that we're talking about, around the Kravica murder and afterward, did you or anyone else you know go back into those woods to retrieve Muslim bodies out of those woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the employees of the public utilities company and the civilian protection gathered bodies. There were even lorries that couldn't access certain areas, but as to whether they were in Ravni Buljim, I don't know, but they did bring them in from the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your people actually went into those woods at that time-frame, with Muslim soldiers running around in those woods, to pick up bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not how it was done in the woods. It was up to the road, as far as the road, as far as the river. But as to the woods, as far as I know, given what I was told, on that day there were no soldiers, no Muslim soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You mentioned -- I believe you mentioned a grave in the area of Halilovici that you didn't have anything to do with. Did you get information about some grave around Halilovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mentioned that a while ago because I don't know which Defence team put a question to me about Momir Nikolic and wanted to know whether I had done that and Momir mentioned me and said that I had told him that we had transported the bodies there and that we had buried them there. That had nothing do with us. That's not what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell me very briefly what information you had about any potential bodies or graves in the area of Halilovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that. I didn't know anything about that, Mr. Prosecutor. Mr. Ruez asked me about that when he went into the field. He asked me about that. I said I knew nothing about it. He didn't even take me to show me where the location was, he just asked me to take him down the Drina River to show him the other grave site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, during your -- the -- about two-hour time at the restaurant with Mr. Borovcanin, was Mr. Borovcanin present at that restaurant the entire time with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you or he mention going back to Kravica -- or going to Kravica to help Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I have understood you very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you or anybody at the table talk about going to Kravica that evening and helping out the Muslims at the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't, and while I was there no one discussed this. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And again, just last question, the men that were killed and buried in 1992 from the Vuk Karadzic School, were they separated from their families and were their families then shipped out to Kladanj back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-161 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 the bodies that we buried by the Drina were the bodies of people who had been detained in the gym of the Vuk Karadzic School, of the Vuk Karadzic primary school. Where they had been brought in from, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. We don't have any further questions for you, sir, which means that your testimony finishes here, ends here. You will receive assistance from our staff to facilitate your return back home at the earliest. I think, as my duty -- no, ask him to put it ... I think it is my duty also on your behalf to thank the various Defence teams that followed Mr. Beara in particular -- that followed Mr. Ostojic in particular for having come forward and succeeded in finishing the cross-examination in time, which makes it possible for you to return back home somewhat earlier. I also thank you for having come over to give testimony, and I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bourgon, Mr. McCloskey. If you are in a position to come back to us on what we discussed in the beginning of today's sitting. If not, we can do it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I must say that at the break we have agreed to disagree on one issue and that is the rebuttal issue. The position of the Defence is as follows: Of course if my colleague qualifies for rebuttal in accordance with the jurisprudence of this Tribunal, then there is nothing the Defence could do about that. As long as he qualifies in accordance with past decisions on rebuttal and that could take place at any moment. But he will have first to qualify for those. If that is the case then we can agree on dates very easily. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we will come back to you tomorrow on -- pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's easier. I think we could decide it here and now, but I think -- yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In thinking about it, Your Honour, I don't -- I don't think the Prosecution wants to stick its neck out and agree to this at all. Out of order now, with possibly no chance of rebutting it, I don't think so. I think we can put that to bed. We absolutely disagree with this coming into our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for your -- first of all for your mutual consultations, as for your cooperation. We will come back to you tomorrow. I don't think it will provide us with any problems to decide. Next -- yeah, we will finish the exhibits now. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We've got the pseudonym sheet, P02485 and then we have, I believe, two pictures of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. I think one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the -- one of them is 65 ter 1553, and the other one is PIC00077, which is the one that was marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Any objections? I hear no objections. They are so admitted. First one will remain -- I think if they have been marked by -- no, it's the first one only, the pseudonym sheet will remain under seal. The rest don't need to be kept like that. Now, Defence teams. Mr. Zivanovic, do you wish to tender the part of the testimony of the witness in --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Page from Blagojevic case, I confronted the witness with this part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I will not mention the page and line number. You all know which one it is because otherwise we'll have to go into private session. I just ask whether the Prosecution objects to this -- the admission of this document. Or, for that matter, any other Defence team. I hear no objections. That is so admitted. And it will remain under seal because otherwise it would expose the identity of the witness. Mr. Ostojic, I do not have notice that you wish to tender documents, but I suppose you may have some.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I -- we do, Your Honour. We weren't sure that it was going to proceed today, but we have a list. We would like to submit into evidence under our exhibits here, it's called 1D168, which was previously placed on e-court, which is the proofing note of the 21st of April, 2004. I think we saw it, we had testimony on that specifically. Also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In whole or in part?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's a one-page document, so I would say whatever the Court's pleasure is on this. We think it is always necessary in part, but if the Court feels it's necessary, it's only a one-page document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The various parts of the OTP interview conducted on the 13th of October, 2000, which was previously identified as 1D167, and then we would also ask for the portions of the transcript of this gentleman's testimony in that other case that we were -- that was in e-court under 1D169, just the portions that he obviously discussed. And then we would ask for the OTP proofing notes of both the 20th of March 2007 as 2D96, and the proofing notes, which is actually a letter dated the 21st of March, 2007, which is 2D86. I don't know why the numbers are different, but I'm going to look into that. But those are the numbers that I have. And in addition to that, we would ask that the two documents that the witness marked during his testimony, which are 2DIC79, where he mentions, I think, the word "volunteer," ultimately. And then also 2DIC80, which is where he mentions the headquarters that Your Honour assisted us with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Are there any objections on your part?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: One last thing, my learned friend and I are working on a specific stipulation relating to one issue that does involve Exhibit 2D86, we just haven't had an opportunity to actually exchange much other than to discuss that, we hope to have that for the Court tomorrow on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, do you have any objections to any of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's unclear to me when he says portions of the transcripts of the testimony of Blagojevic, that -- that could be a lot of things. And portions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Marked portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't know what he means, and I don't know what "portions of the OTP interview" means. If -- if they are significant portions, and the Court wishes, we'll -- you can see the whole thing. But I think trying to figure out piecemeal is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, fair enough. We are running short of time. I think you will update Mr. McCloskey on that between today and tomorrow. And we will conclude on your exhibits tomorrow. Mr. Stojanovic wishes to tender three documents. One is a photograph of the Kravica warehouse, one is the Bratunac health centre patient log that we saw, and the other one is the RS Republika Srpska MUP magazine where we saw the photos of those four policemen. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, in fact I would join in the Bratunac health centre. He's stolen that from us, but no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So they are -- any objections on the part of any of the Defence teams? None. So these three documents are so admitted. And I think we can adjourn now and tomorrow we'll start with finalising the Beara Defence exhibits. Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Just one quick point, Mr. President, concerning if the Trial Chamber is about to render a decision with respect to hearing a Defence expert at this time, both my colleague and I from the Prosecution, we agreed on the 14 days, 14 days after the hearing of the witness. However, can 14 days -- if the witness testifies on the 23rd of May, that would give that we would have to file a response on the 5th or 6th of June, which is in the middle of the week that the Trial Chamber is not sitting. So then we will be asking at least to file our response after the week that the Trial Chamber is not sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will take that into consideration when we discuss tomorrow. One other thing that I want to be sure that you have been informed that the Friday -- sitting this Friday has been moved to the morning. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of March, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
